text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
-- PUBLIC SECURITIES ARE GOOD BUSINESS FOR BANKS

Many of the most solid and traditional banks acquired state and municipal bonds because they found to be a good deal, says Manoel Felix Cintra Neto, president of Brazil's largest future exchange BM&F and head of local bank Banco Multiplic.
-- COFAP TO BUILD PLANT IN TENNESSEE
Brazil's Cofap has chosen the location of the plant it plans to build in the United States: Kings Port, Tennessee.
Brazil's strategy to stretch the maturity period of its public debt includes the launch of a 15-year Treasury paper.

Part of the money that Paulo Cesar Farias, former campaign manager of ex-President Fernando Collor, raised is in the hands of the Italian Mafia. Farias was a key figure behind a corruption ring that exchanged government favours for money. The revelations led to Collor's resignation in 1992.
-- RAINS IN SALVADOR KILL NINE PEOPLE
Heavy rains over the weekend have killed nine and left at least 70 people homeless in Salvador in the northeastern state of Bahia.
The Federal Police said it was investigating the methods used by the Landless Movement (MST) to maintain discipline in the camps.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
